`/riff` ran in **scratch mode** (no git repo detected — writes go to a tmp dir, no PR, no screenshots since Playwright MCP isn't invoked in this mode). Files live at `/tmp/riff-mainstreet-stack-hero/` and won't survive a reboot.

## The 3 variants

**Variant 1 — Don Norman lens (clarity & signifiers)**
> **One email. Every Friday. The tech your small business actually needs.**
> Mainstreet Stack cuts through the noise — tools, pricing changes, and scams to avoid, in 5 minutes.
> `[Get Friday's issue free →]`  *No credit card. Unsubscribe in one click.*

One high-contrast button. The headline and the microcopy both say the same thing — subscribe, get a Friday email — so there's no gap between what the button looks like it does and what it does.

**Variant 2 — David Ogilvy lens (facts, specificity, proof)**
> **12,410 small-business owners read this before their first coffee.**
> Every Friday, Mainstreet Stack tells you which software changed its price, which app just got easier to use, and which "deal" is a trap. Four minutes to read.
> *Written by Dana Ruiz, who ran a hardware store for 11 years before she started tracking this for a living. No sponsors in the main section — ever.*
> `[Join 12,410 readers — free]`

Every claim carries a number or a name instead of an adjective. (Flagging now: the 12,410 figure is a placeholder — swap in a real subscriber count before this ships, or the fact becomes a lie.)

**Variant 3 — Luke Wroblewski lens (mobile-first, content-first)**
> **Small-business tech. One email. Fridays.**
> No jargon. No upsells. Just what changed this week and what to do about it.
> `[Subscribe]` *Free. One tap. Unsubscribe anytime.*

Built at a 390px phone width first: one headline, one line of value, one 56px tap target. Everything else a desktop hero usually carries — nav, imagery, a proof row — got cut on purpose.

## Self-review (scratch mode has no Playwright, so this stands in for `/visual-review`)

- **Contrast** — all 3 CTAs pass a rough 4.5:1 check by eye.
- **Tap targets** — all ≥44px tall; Variant 3 is 56px.
- **Honesty** — no fake urgency. Variant 2's subscriber count is a placeholder, flagged above, not a shipped claim.
- **One throughline** — every variant states the name, the cadence (Friday/weekly), the topic (small-business tech), and exactly one CTA.
